## Natural history notes

A small bee fly characterized by a fuzzy bee-like body, clear to lightly patterned wings, hovering flight, and a long stiff proboscis used to reach nectar while visiting flowers. In Florida, Bombylius mexicanus has been recorded in the state, including north-central Florida, and is most likely found in sunny open or semi-open habitats such as sandhills, pine flatwoods, roadsides, gardens, and wildflower patches. Adults feed on nectar and can act as pollinators, while the larvae of Bombylius bee flies are generally parasitoids or nest associates of solitary bees and wasps, developing in or near host nests rather than feeding on plants.
